description_full: Toyota Tsusho Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, engages in the manufacturing, processing, and sale of various products in Japan and internationally. It operates through Metal+ (Plus), Circular Economy, Supply Chain, Mobility, Green Infrastructure, Digital Solutions, Lifestyle, and Africa segments. The company processes, manufactures, and sells automotive steel and aluminum sheets, special and stainless steel sheets, electrical steel sheets, and steel bars and pipes, as well as building materials; and develops, sells, and distributes critical metals, batteries, electronic materials, synthetic resins, rubber, organic chemicals, additives, and pharmaceutical raw materials. It also procures, designs, develops, sells, and services mobility interior and exterior parts and accessories, as well as offers logistics, airport management, resources recycling, and supply chain-related business development services; and import and exports commercial, passenger, industrial, and other vehicles and supply parts, as well as provides vehicle installation and assembly services. In addition, the company trades in manufacturing and logistics equipment, parts and tools, and construction machineries, as well as develops social infrastructure and operates power generation plants, airports, and ports; and sells electronic devices and components, semiconductors, IT-related products, computers, peripherals, and software, as well as offers network construction and maintenance, help desk, cybersecurity, and software development. Further, it is involved in the import and export of grain, agricultural, livestock, and marine products, as well as provision of insurance agency and brokerage services, textiles and fiber products, real estate development and management, and healthcare centers; and leasing and sale of new and used cars, after-sale services, sale of pharmaceutical products, and retail business. The company was founded in 1936 and is headquartered in Nagoya, Japan.

financial_summary: Toyota Tsusho Corp. is a large-cap industrials business with a $39.3B market cap on $72.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +2% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.

Returns on capital run at 9% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, and 11% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $1.7B in free cash flow — roughly 2 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.24× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.9× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 8.7×.

Shareholder yield is only 1.9%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

Tariff and trade-policy exposure — industrial exporters sit squarely in the crosshairs of protectionist policy, and retaliatory tariffs can close markets without warning.

news_headlines.title: Toyota Tsusho Corp. - Unsponsored ADR (TYHOY) Is a Great Choice for 'Trend' Investors, Here's Why

sect: Its 5% operating margin is roughly in line with the Industrials median (9%).
It captures well under its share of sector profits (0.43x its revenue share).
It accounts for 1.9% of sector revenue and 0.8% of sector operating profit.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.01 across 548 companies in the universe; the top four hold 9% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 34% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 6% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 18% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 64% and a beta of 1.07, it moves roughly with the market.
Trading is thin (about $382K a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.
val: The stock trades 36% below its DCF fair value of $32.87, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 18%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $21.74 to $50.30 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Industrials peers: P/E 15.4 vs 24.1 and EV/EBITDA 2.0 vs 13.4 (sector median).
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 4.4% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 0.2% (vs the 8% bar).
The price implies 3.1% annual cash-flow growth, 7pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 9% earns above the cost of capital of 8.3%, but the 1pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have been steady (CV 0.06).
It runs a 11% gross margin and converts 2% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.24x.
ROE of 12% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.7x equity multiplier).
SG&A jumped 17% last year, worth watching.
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.9x net debt to EBITDA ($9.3B of cash against $13.6B of debt), with interest covered 8.7x.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 1.8% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 57% of profits supports about 5.4% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.0%), and institutions hold 0%.
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.9% (0.0% in buybacks and 1.8% in dividends).
people: With about 74,927 employees, each generates about $966K of revenue, 2.7x the Industrials median.
That works out to $23K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.7M (2x revenue per employee).
